items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I don't know. Temperament. I got along beautifully with him... My job was to hold at that level... I didn't want no drum solo

ctx.x: I don't know. Temperament. I got along beautifully with him, but he wasn't good for a bunch of guy's organization because he would create a lot of little disturbances. He wasn't -- and the thing about Duke's band we had a band of individual stars. They could stand on their own. On their own two feet, but as a team, they were just like this. My job with the Duke Ellington band, I didn't go

and things. in for all them Buddy Rich solos/. My job was to hold at that level, because you take a band today, they'll start up playing down here and when they wind up, they're playing up here, so fast. Notice it, just notice it. Not that they want to do it.

But invariably they'll accelarate, every one of them, all of them, and we had a band of all-stars. The way they started off, that's the way they end. That was the thing, (Laughter) my job was to keep them turkeys. I didn't want no drum solo, I could imitate anybody. I could do it, but I know it wasn't no good for the band.
